newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 14.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
RAJIV GANDHI NAMED PRIME ACCUSED IN BOFORS CASE

Highly placed sources in the Cabinet Secretariat said former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi was named as the prime accused in a proposed chargesheet relating to the 14.37 billion rupees Bofors gun deal. The sources said Central Bureau of Intelligence director Joginder Singh has sent the Bofors chargesheet for the government's formal clearance. The chargesheet holds Rajiv Gandhi -- he was assassinated in May 1991 while campaigning -- guilty of hatching a conspiracy to cause wilful loss to the state exchequer and allowing middlemen in the gun deal, but failed to prove he benefited financially himself.
The Times Of India
PRIME MINISTER CALLS BLUFF ON ARMY PRESENCE IN KASHMIR

The Indian prime minister has ruled out the withdrawal of security forces from Jammu and Kashmir, suggested by his Pakistani counterpart Nawaz Sharif. Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said the question of setting up a joint working group (JWG) on Kashmir would be considered by the foreign secretaries of the two countries. Replying to a question, he said the security forces in Kashmir were responding to particular situation and when their task was complete, the situation might be reviewed. He added the situation in the state was of Pakistan's making.
The Economic Times
NO MORE GIFTS TO SHAREHOLDERS

The new Companies Bill will bar companies from giving gifts at shareholders' meetings and ban shareholders' accepting gifts. Violation of the rule would attract fines up to 10 times the value of the gift given, demanded or accepted. The section barring gifts do not form part of the provisions relating to annual general meetings but was inserted in a section dealing with the manner and time of payment of dividends.
NATIONAL BOURSE LISTS FIRMS CHARGED WITH FRAUD

The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has released a list of 39 individuals and firms against whom complaints were lodged with the police for perpetrating fraud in the stock markets. The cases pertained to introduction of fake or duplicate shares in the market, non-payment of dues and cheating of bourse members. The NSE released another list of 61 investors against whom only police complaints were lodged. Most of these complaints were filed by NSE members. This was the first time any bourse had come out with a list of individuals or firms who have defrauded members or brokers.
WORSENING INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS AFFECT PHILIPS OUTPUT

Bitten by competition and worsening industrial relations, Philips India Ltd continued to produce at capacity utilisation of around 20 percent at its consumer electronics unit in Calcutta. In fact, worsening industrial relations at Philips' Calcutta factories were likely to cause embarrassment for the consumer electronics giant at its annual general meeting. Peeved by the suspension of some of its front-ranking union leaders recently, Philips workers in Calcutta planned to organise a major agitation programme at the AGM venue.
Financial Express
RBI TO INTRODUCE 14-DAY TREASURY BILLS VIA AUCTION ROUTE

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is all set to introduce 14-day treasury bills through the auction route. The paper would qualify for repo facilities. The RBI would also introduce the 273-day treasury bill in the money market. It had however decided not to go ahead with floating proposed seven-day and 182-day treasury bills for the time being. The 14-day instrument would have a notified amount and its auction might be held every Friday. The notified amount would vary with each auction, depending on the liquidity condition in the money market.
STATE BANK SUBSIDIARIES TO TAP MARKET

The seven associate banks of the State Bank of India (SBI) planned to tap the capital market in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) even though the government had failed to amend the SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act. The actual premiums might vary according to the financial strength of the subsidiary concerned and market conditions. The associate banks, which were finding it difficult to expand business due to capital constraints, now plan to go ahead with the issues even if the Act were not amended. Under the Act, only the SBI, state governments, public corporations, cooperatives and trustee bodies could hold more than 200 shares.
GOVERNMENT READY TO BUILD BANGALORE AIRPORT

The civil aviation minister announced that the state-owned Airport Authority of India was ready to build an international airport at Bangalore if the Tata group-led consortium was unwilling to construct it on a build own transfer (BOT) basis. The Tata group had originally proposed building the 15 billion rupee airport on a build-own-operate format.
Business Standard
BILL BANS FOREIGN STAKE IN TERRESTRIAL BROADCASTING

The Broadcast Bill to be introduced in parliament will bar foreign participation in terrestrial broadcasts. It will also empower the proposed broadcast authority to invite bids for licences for direct-to-home (DTH) services. The DTH provider and other service providers would have to convince the authority that a transponder would be available and obtain technical clearance from the wireless advisor to the government. The bill would also demand all service providers to uplink from India.
NEW PROVISIONING TO COST BANKS SEVEN BLN RUPEES

Banks would have to provide for an additional seven billion rupees in their balance sheets as a result of a new RBI directive on provisioning norms for non-performing assets. Calculations by senior bank officials revealed that the provisioning variation would be 10 to 15 percent of the current provisions. The new norms would affect the bottom lines of most banks. Banks that had just made marginal profits would be hurt the most. The directive, asking banks to make good the difference between the provision made by them and the assessment of the RBI, has upset many banks.
HEWLETT PACKARD TO PULL OUT OF JOINT HCL JOINT VENTURE

Hewlett Packard (HP) has decided to pull out of its infotech joint venture with HCL Corporation. HP would sell its entire 26 percent stake to the HCL group. But distribution of HCL-HP products as well as HP's exclusive products in the country would continue to be carried out by HCL. The HCL group holds a 50 percent stake in HCL-HP while HP controls 26 percent. The public and financial institutions hold the remaining 24 percent. HCL-HP has a equity base of 300 million rupees.
GOVERNMENT MULLING MARUTI STAKE SELL OFF

The government is considering the possibility of selling its entire 50 percent stake in Maruti Udyog to its joint venture partner, Suzuki Motors. The proposal was mooted because of a recent government decision to gradually move out of non-core sectors. However, a final decision by the government on the politically sensitive issue was not expected in the near future. Sources said the government would be willing to consider its total withdrawal from its venture only after the car market in the country matured with increased competition.
U.S. FIRM MARKS INFRASTRUCTURE FUND FOR INDIAN EQUITY

American International Group (AIG) has earmarked about 30 percent of its $2 billion Asian Infrastructure Fund-II (AIF-II) for equity investments in India. The allocation from AIF-II would be around $600-700 million. AIG had also earmarked 30-35 percent of an infrastructure bond fund for investments in India, which would also be about 600-700 million. The AIF-II allocation would lead two other new equity funds designated for investments in India.
The Observer
MAHARASHTRA TO PICK UP 30 PCT STAKE IN DABHOL POWER CO

The Maharashtra government will opt for 30 percent equity participation, worth about 4.7 billion rupees, in the Dabhol Power Company (DPC). DPC is a joint venture in which Enron Corp owns 80 percent of the project, with GE Capital and Bechtel Enterprises holding 10 percent each. The state electricity board would buy equity worth 70-100 million rupees and the rest would be distributed among other statutory corporations of Maharashtra.
INDIA, PAKISTAN PROTEST AGAINST U.S. BAN ON SHRIMP IMPORTS

India and Pakistan have complained to World Trade Organisation (WTO) about a United States' ban on wild harvested shrimp imports. The two countries asked the WTO to constitute a panel to look into their complaint as the U.S. ban had nullified the free trade benefits and violated the procedures of the multilateral trade organisation. India argued that the U.S. ban on shrimp imports from countries without certified conservation measures for sea turtles was extraterritorial, arbitrary and discriminatory. India said it had no objections to countries implementing environmental measures within their territories and that it supported sea turtle conservation efforts.
NO IMPACT OF GRAND MET-GUINNESS MERGER NOW ON INDIAN FIRMS

The merger of two U.K.-based food and drinks giants, Grand Metropolitan (Grand Met) and Guinness, has led to confusion about the status of their Indian liquor business operations. Grand Met clarified that Indian operations would continue as usual and compete with each other. Grand Met's liquor arm has a joint venture with Polychem in India, while Guinness' liquor division has a joint venture with United Breweries. The future of these two joint venture companies is uncertain. With four companies involved, two of them Indian, legal problems were expected to crop up.
MMTC STEEL PROJECT GETS GO AHEAD

The government has approved a 15.1 billion rupee integrated steel project promoted by state-owned MMTC to produce 110,000 tonnes of steel annually. The project, called Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd (NINL), would produce 492,000 tonnes of pig iron, 276,000 tonnes of billets and 300,000 tonnes of wire rods in its first phase. About 2.45 billion rupees would be raised through public or private placement. International investors, including Lucky Goldstar of South Korea, would put up 1.3 billion rupees towards the equity. Australian coal companies and foreign investors would contribute 700 million to the equity of the coke oven project.
